title: Weak and strong duality, complementary slackness

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A water utility solves a maximization LP. An analyst has a feasible plan worth 820 and a set of dual feasible prices that prove a bound of 860. She has not solved the LP. What can she conclude?

options.text: The optimum is exactly 840, halfway between the two numbers
options.says: Weak duality only brackets the optimum; it says nothing about where inside the bracket it lies.

options.text: The plan is within 40 of the optimum, which may lie above it
options.says: Right: no plan beats a dual feasible bound, and the optimum is at least the plan's value, so the gap is at most 40.

options.text: The plan is optimal, since the bound proves nothing beats it
options.says: A plan is certified only when its value equals a bound; here 820 is below 860.

options.text: The prices are wrong, since a valid bound equals a plan's value
options.says: Dual feasible prices can prove a loose bound: pricing every cash row at 0.66 proved 5,207.4, far above every plan.

origin.section: Weak Duality: No Plan Is Worth More Than Any Covering Prices' Bound

questions.stem: A planner raises a minimum-delivery requirement so far that the primal LP reports INFEASIBLE. Before the change, both the primal and its dual solved to optimality. She now solves the dual of the changed model. What should the dual report?

options.text: Optimal, since the dual's cover rows contain no right-hand sides
options.says: The old prices do stay feasible, but a feasible dual of an infeasible primal cannot be optimal; its bound falls without end.

options.text: Infeasible, since an infeasible primal always has an infeasible dual
options.says: Not always: the floor-900 prices stayed dual feasible when the floor rose to 2,000.

options.text: Optimal with value 0, since a model with no plan has a zero bound
options.says: There is no finite optimum: the dual's bound can be pushed down without limit.

options.text: Unbounded, since the old prices stay feasible and no plan limits the bound
options.says: Right: the cover rows do not depend on right-hand sides, so the dual is still feasible, and with no primal plan its bound can fall without end.

origin.section: Strong Duality: At the Optimum the Two Values Are Equal

questions.stem: At the optimum of a warehouse's maximization LP, the row 'forklift hours at most 300' has 45 hours of slack, and the variable 'night shifts' has the value 12. What must the optimal prices satisfy?

options.text: The forklift price is 0, and the night-shift reduced cost is 0
options.says: Right: a row with slack has price 0, and a variable in use has reduced cost 0.

options.text: The forklift price is 45, and the night-shift reduced cost is 12
options.says: Slack and value are not prices; complementary slackness makes the products zero, so a nonzero slack forces a zero price.

options.text: The forklift price is 45, and the night-shift reduced cost is 0
options.says: The forklift row has slack, so its price must be 0: slack times price is 0, and 45 is the slack, not a price.

options.text: The forklift price is 0, and the night-shift reduced cost is 12
options.says: Night shifts are in use, so their reduced cost must be 0; 12 is the variable's value, not its reduced cost.

origin.section: Complementary Slackness: Slack Rows Have Price Zero, Used Variables Have Reduced Cost Zero
